STEP 1 - Vessel type: a flat, square-ish white plate with a raised rim band and a flat centre. No inner wall, so it is a flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: a square dinner plate is typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large relative to the side plate on the left, so I estimate about 26 cm.
b) Reference: the salad plate on the left is about 18-20 cm across. The main plate is roughly 1.3 times its width, so about 25 cm. The rim of the main plate is roughly 6 to 7 lengths of the corn cob (about 4 cm each), which again suggests about 25 cm.
Final width: 25 cm square, area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items (flat layer, estimated thickness):
- Caesar-style romaine salad with dressing and croutons: covers about 30% of the plate, about 190 cm². Loose leaves, about 4 cm thick at the mound. Average about 2 cm. Volume = 190 x 2 = 380 ml. Dressed chopped greens at 0.6 g/ml gives about 230 g.
- Breaded fish fillet (top right): about 12% of the plate, about 75 cm² (roughly 10 x 7.5 cm). Thickness about 2 cm. Volume = 150 ml x 1.0 = about 150 g.
- Glazed meat pieces with orange zest (right): about 10% of the plate, about 60 cm². Thickness about 2 cm. Volume = 120 ml x 1.0 = about 120 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no clear base layer beneath the toppings. The salad mound is the main hidden bulk, already counted. Side salad and corn on the left plate are a separate vessel and are excluded.

STEP 5 - Energy density (as served):
- Caesar salad with dressing and croutons: about 150 kcal per 100 g (dressing and croutons add energy).
- Breaded fish: about 200 kcal per 100 g (breading and frying).
- Glazed meat with zest: about 210 kcal per 100 g (sugar glaze and fat).

Totals: about 500 g of food, roughly 0.15 x 230 + 0.2 x 150 + 0.21 x 120 ≈ 35 + 30 + 25 ≈ 890 kcal for the main plate.
